item.title: Riot Games — Visual Systems & UX
item.description:
Selected work prepared for Riot Games — Visual Systems & UX.

A curated selection rather than a complete archive. The pieces are chosen to show one through-line: how visual systems create emotional and experiential cohesion across every player-facing surface. Live broadcast overlay systems engineered against in-game UI, self-serve template kits that hold brand voice without a designer in the loop, motion-graphic families designed once and scaled across an ecosystem, and worldbuilding craft that gives those systems something to be cohesive around.

item.title: Back2Warcraft Twitch Emote — B2WRip
item.description:
B2WRip is a Twitch emote made for the Back2Warcraft channel, the long-running shoutcasting home for Warcraft III esports. The mark is built to be readable at Twitch’s tiny emote sizes (28px, 56px, 112px) while still carrying the channel’s visual personality, so it lands in chat the moment a play goes south.

Designed as part of an ongoing graphics package for B2W, alongside a paired animated shoutout sequence that triggers on stream when the emote gets spammed during a moment of dramatic loss. The animation extends the emote into a short on-broadcast beat that closes the loop between chat and the show itself.

item.title: The Ash Keepers — Season 22
item.description: A set of four original avatars designed for the Back2Warcraft Twitch community to support the W3Champions Season 22 Finals. Each avatar reframes a classic Warcraft 3 hero — Pit Lord, Warden, Paladin, Beastmaster — as an Ash Keeper: a spectral guardian tasked with restoring the living flame. Available through Matcherino; purchases pooled directly into the tournament prize.

item.title: Back2Warcraft Twitch Emote — B2WBoat
item.description:
B2WBoat is a Twitch emote built for the Back2Warcraft channel. Like the rest of the B2W emote family, it has to do its job at 28, 56, and 112 pixel sizes, so the silhouette and color blocking carry most of the work. The artwork sits in the channel’s running visual language alongside the other shoutcaster-specific emotes used during Warcraft III broadcasts.

Part of an ongoing graphics package for Back2Warcraft that mixes overlay coverlay assets, emote families, and animated shoutouts so the channel reads as one cohesive show across chat, overlay, and stream.

item.title: Elite Grubby Guard (2025 Remaster)
item.description: A 2025 remaster of the original Elite Grubby Guard piece first released in 2012 to celebrate Grubby’s MLG run. Same core identity — Grubby as an Elite Protoss Stalker — with refreshed linework, updated palette, and a composition optimized for current broadcast and social formats.

item.title: Commission: Gentle Avatar
item.description:
Stormbolt to the FACE – Gentle WC3’s Avatar Commission

Awesome player, streamer, and all-around good human, Gentle reached out for a custom WC3 Champions avatar—and I couldn’t have been happier to answer the call.

He was super kind and professional throughout, and one thing that really made this commission special was the involvement of his girlfriend. She’s an artist too, and the piece she created for him was not only fantastic but hugely inspiring as I explored the right angle and energy for the Mountain King.

item.title: Esports Broadcast Graphics
item.description: Half a decade of professional esports broadcast work. Stream overlays, event splashes, and in-game graphic systems for Team Liquid (StarCraft 2, Dota 2), Team Grubby, Back2Warcraft, Victorious Gaming, and the Warcraft 3 community. Broadcast graphics demand a specific discipline: dense information presented in a readable hierarchy that never upstages the game itself.

item.title: Twitch Icon - Arbiter
item.description:
I tackled what I thought was going to be a much more simple task.  Taking a Starcraft 1 arbiter and making a Twitch icon out of it for a well known Starcraft 2 player.  Being that the Starcraft assets where already quite small, I assumed that resizing it a little smaller wouldn’t be to bad an approach.

To be honest it wasn’t bad, but I wasn’t satisfied with the muddy result, so I decided to do a rough redraw of the image to simplify it a bit, This was it stand out a bit more when sized down.

item.title: BaseTradeTV Reflection
item.description: Though I am mired in my current work, I find that it can be a good thing to take small breaks from the grind to reignite my passion for artistic work by tackling smaller more focused projects.  I enjoy doing overlay and eSports work for many reasons, but one of the them is that it utilizes a generally very simple concepts that can be deeply explored through creative problem solving and intelligent design.  This allows me to push aside a lot of the extra considerations that can weigh down exploration of design while I’m working on such a complicated project as my Indie game Mecromage.

item.title: League Champ Select Overlay
item.description:
A friend of mine, Eryn is an up and coming League of Legends caster.  He has been working daily to bring some eSports action to scene with his heated play by plays and intuitive analysis.  His casting chops far outweigh the production quality of the overlay he was using, so I decided I’d lend a hand in hopes of giving his casts the unique flavor they deserve.

It’s no dramatic departure from LoL themes, but its a fun and colorful overlay that I enjoyed putting together in a relatively small amount of time.  It would be fun to explore creating an out of game overlay and in game overlay as well.

item.title: IdrA Logo Reflection
item.description: About a year ago I had the pleasure of working with Greg ‘IrdA’ Fields on his solo brand logo.  He was one of the most responsive and engaging clients I’ve had the pleasure of working with.  The logo processes went smoothly. Though a bit on the long side, we both ensured IrdA was getting a logo that would hit all his key branding goals. We started out by getting the right look and feel for is name.  We veered away from using symbols or abstractions to convey his Brand, after all IdrA was IdrA.  The name had a cool symmetrical and simple look, so we pursued that line of thinking when developing the core Logo. After the this main lettering element was settled, we thought it would be enjoyable to embellish the design with a cheeky cartoon ‘Graken’.  A fan calling card of his.

item.title: Cheerful–Grubby Melting Face
item.description:
Though I still am quite the nomad currently, I’m very happy to be able to take a moment of respite from time to time.  Today I’m thankful for my laptop, Wacom tablet, and being blessed with the opportunity to watch Grubby 2-0 incumbent Polt at Dreamhack 2013. Way to go Grubby, you’ve brightened yet another fan’s day!

item.title: Grubby vs Flash MLG Dallas Cheerful
item.description:
[HD 1280x720] [HD + 1920x1050]

I found out that Grubby will be squaring off vs  Flash in the first casted match of  MLG Dallas – Summer Championship happening tomorrow! The Warcraft 3 legend and Starcraft 2 titan squaring off inspired me to sketch up a little cheerful for them. I’m cheering for Grubby, of course but I wish the best of luck to both players. Somewhat selfishly I hope that it will be one of the most devastating spectacles of Terran mechanized battle bombardment thundering against the devote zen psi-shielding of the focused Protoss as they lighten the field with their searing storms.

item.title: SC2Pro Stream Front
item.description:
I was commissioned to do a budget web splash page.  The purpose -to have a stream front that fans can navigate to and see multiple streams simultaneously in action, from a given team or group.  The challenge - to create a design in three hours.  While I accomplished the initial three hours concept goal, I did spend another three refining some of the ideas.

item.title: Grubby – How’s the Weather?
item.description:
How’s the Weather Wallpaper - Full size link

It is finally finished.  I’ve been working for several months touch and go on this T-shirt concept for Starcraft 2 eSports Progamer, Manuel ‘Grubby’ Schenkhuizen.  I has been fun and challenging to create a fictional character that can summon lightening attacks at a whim.  There are many things I’d love to keep fixing up on the project, but I have to call it ‘done’ at some point.

item.title: Team Eve Gaming Logo
item.description:
Creating Team Eve’s logo was a rewarding experience, and a test of the process of achieving a shared vision with a client.  Below I discuss the process I used to communicate online, across the globe, to deliver not only a logo for an up and coming eSports team, but some working assets for their web and streaming needs.

PHASE 1 - INTENT

Establish Intent - The above image compiled the sources that I asked the client bring to me as direction on how we might evaluate their personal tastes for their design and their intent.  I want the final product to represent as best as possible the client’s unique identity as well as resolve their professional needs.

item.title: Grubby Splash Protoss Video Player
item.description:
A web page splash page for a the work in progress FollowGrubby.com.

I originally took in game screen-shots to construct an image that would serve as backdrop for Grubby’s announcement to his fans.  Wanting to add more personality, I decided to illustrate my own Protoss UI over the top of the draft, and it came out much better than I had anticipated.

In the end, I actually also created the .html css file for the live splash page.  It took a little bit of learning on top of what I already know, but after about 30 minutes I had the file that would go live. I was quite proud of myself.
